subject: COBOL character repertoire (encoding of, mapping of, substitute graphics)
notes: A.1 item 25 (required + documented): docs/CONFORMANCE.md DOC-A.1-25 states the mapping (ISO/IEC 10646 code points held as UTF-16, one set for the alphanumeric and the national class), the source-text encoding and the absence of substitute graphics. cite.py --check 8.1.3.2 'The implementor shall define a mapping of each basic letter, basic digit, basic special' -> OK 8.1.3.2 1); --check 8.1.3.2 'substitute graphics' -> OK 8.1.3.2 5). The encoding disposition is implemented in SourceTextDecoder.Decode and nowhere else: a byte-order mark names the encoding (UTF-8, UTF-16 LE/BE, UTF-32 LE/BE) and is not source text; a marked file not well-formed in its encoding is the error COBOL5434 naming the file and byte offset (no fallback, the mark states the encoding); an unmarked file is UTF-8 or, when not well-formed UTF-8, ISO/IEC 8859-1 (every byte its own code point, so FUNCTION ORD of the byte 0xE9 is 234) with the warning COBOL5435. No byte is replaced by U+FFFD (the previous decoder printed 65534 for ORD of a Latin-1 e-acute with no diagnostic). Re-probed on this tree before the fix: ORD 65534 for the unmarked file and for the marked file; after: 234 with COBOL5435, and COBOL5434 for the marked file. The rule-1 precedence (ISO silent, GnuCOBOL passes source bytes through unchanged) is the DOC row's reason for Latin-1. Witnesses: the accepted golden reads a library text holding the raw byte, the refused golden a library text with a UTF-8 mark and the same byte; SourceTextDecoderTests cover every mark, the offsets, lone surrogates, the UTF-32 range and the once-per-file reporting. kb/Work PB1397. retired-witness: src/WiseOwl.Cobol.Frontend/Pipeline/CompilationInputs.cs#ReadAllText (CompilationInputs.ReadAllText no longer exists: the bytes of a source or library text become characters in SourceTextDecoder.Decode, read through CompilationInputs.ReadSourceText (kb/Work PB1397))
